language.heading: Language
language.label: Display language
language.description: The language Roxy's own interface is written in. It does not change how the agent talks to you — ask it in whatever language you like, in the chat.
language.translatedBy: Translations are community-maintained and may lag behind English.

workstreams.heading: Workstreams
workstreams.autoTitle: New sessions get their own workstream
workstreams.autoDescription: Each session works in its own git worktree on its own branch, so parallel sessions can't overwrite each other or fight with your editor. The folder is created on the session's first message, and only in git repositories. Turn this off to run new sessions directly in the project folder.
workstreams.prefixDescription: New workstreams get a branch named after the session. This is what goes in front of it — use your initials, wip, or clear it for no prefix at all.
workstreams.prefixFootnote: Only affects new workstreams. Existing branches keep their names — rename one from the bar under the composer.

browser.heading: Browser
browser.title: Roxy browser
browser.description: Opens a persistent browser the agent shares. Sign in to sites here once — your session (cookies/logins) is saved, so the agent can act with your access.
browser.cookiesDescription: Read, edit, import and delete the browser's cookies — the built-in equivalent of the Cookie-Editor extension. Import and export use its JSON format, so a blob copied out of Chrome pastes straight in. To work on just one site, use the cookie button in the browser's own toolbar.

webSearch.heading: Web search
webSearch.title: Exa API key (optional)
webSearch.description: The websearch tool works out of the box on Exa's free public endpoint. Add a key to lift rate limits.

backup.heading: Backup & restore
backup.title: Skills & MCP servers
backup.description: Export your global skills and MCP server configs to a single file, then import it on another computer to set it up the same way. Importing overwrites skills/servers that share a name.
backup.warning: Heads up: the file includes any MCP secrets (headers/env) in plain text — keep it private.

privacy.heading: Privacy
privacy.title: Send anonymous usage data
privacy.description: Counts and timings — app launches, finished turns, how many steps and tools a turn took, how many tokens it used and roughly what it cost — tied to a random id generated on this machine. Never your prompts, your code, file paths, repo names, or any error text.
privacy.labels: A few labels ride along, and each is matched against a fixed list built into the app: which provider served a turn (a custom endpoint is only ever recorded as “other”), which model family ran (“claude-sonnet”, never the exact model id), which built-in tools ran (an MCP server's own name is only ever recorded as “mcp”), and which kind of error ended a failed turn. It is the only way we can tell whether a release helped or broke things.

update.devMode: Auto-updates run in the installed app.

danger.heading: Danger zone
danger.resetDescription: Wipes all providers, sessions, loops, and settings, then returns to onboarding. This can't be undone.
